documented: OpenRouter authenticates with confidential API keys carried as Authorization Bearer tokens; its authentication guide warns against publishing keys.

The key-creation response returns plaintext key only at creation and separates it from data.hash, masked labels and user/workspace identifiers. Its key example has sk-or-v1- followed by 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.
OpenRouter explicitly publishes sk-or-v1- followed by 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters as the format recognized by its own Secrets guardrail.
assumptions: Positive and negative labels assert the offline detection contract, not issuance, active authorization, exhaustive provider-format conformance, or production precision/recall.

Only the plaintext value is scanned. Attribute names, online authentication, and blanket decoding are not used; no public model IDs, key identifiers, masked display values, or unprefixed hashes are attributed as this secret type.

Case-sensitive provider prefixes, an ASCII word boundary on the left, and the shared native token boundary on the right are conservative scanning constraints. Right-adjacent ASCII letters, digits, underscore, plus, slash, equals, dot, and hyphen prevent accepting only a prefix of a longer token.
No entropy or minimum-digit requirement is imposed because no provider issuance requirement for it was established.
The provider-published guardrail format and creation example support this detection shape, not a complete issuer-generation specification. Other formats are not declared invalid.

The expression is independently written from provider documentation and uses native boundaries. Titus was consulted as a candidate reference, but its case-insensitivity, entropy threshold and min_digits filter are not imported.
evidence.fixture_method: Deterministic synthetic hexadecimal sequences were hand-selected at the documented scanner width, including a digit-free body to avoid inventing a min_digits requirement. Bare and Bearer copies, one-character length/alphabet/case mutations, token adjacency, masked labels, public model IDs and unprefixed hashes exercise detection only. No provider sample key was copied or authenticated.

documented: Groq directs users to generate API keys in its console and keep them in environment variables or a secret manager, not frontend bundles or committed source.
Groq security-onboarding examples use gsk_your_secret_key_here and gsk_..., establishing a secret-bearing gsk_ prefix but not a complete body grammar.
Groq security guidance explicitly identifies key/service IDs as non-secret logging metadata, distinct from confidential API keys.

The 50-54 ASCII alphanumeric body constraint is adapted from Titus v1.2.9 pkg/rule/rules/groq.yml (np.groq.1), with the native right boundary replacing its terminal word boundary. This conservative supported subset is a scanner policy, not issuer-format evidence; the provider docs do not establish this range.
No assertion is made that a candidate satisfying the scanner body range was issued or that a different body width is impossible.
evidence.fixture_method: Hand-selected deterministic ASCII alphanumeric sequence, using 50- and 54-character bodies to exercise both candidate-range boundaries. Bare and Bearer-carried positives and 49-/55-character, alphabet, prefix-case, adjacency, placeholder and public-identifier negatives are synthetic offline candidates, not copied Titus example keys or provider credentials.

documented: xAI API keys authenticate requests as HTTP Bearer tokens and are scoped to teams and permissions.

The management API returns the full apiKey only at creation, separately from apiKeyId and redactedApiKey. The documented full-key example uses xai- followed by an 80-character alphanumeric body; redacted examples use xai-...oYZ4 and xai-a**b.

No entropy or minimum-digit requirement is imposed because no provider issuance requirement for it was established.

The 80-character ASCII alphanumeric/underscore body is adapted from TruffleHog v3.97.4 pkg/detectors/xai/xai.go, replacing the terminal word boundary with the native right boundary. The provider example supports that width, but no exhaustive issuer grammar or generator was established; underscore acceptance is an explicit scanner constraint.
The rule detects only this prefixed API-key candidate shape, not management bearer tokens, public API-key identifiers, or other token revisions.
evidence.fixture_method: Hand-selected deterministic 80-character alphanumeric body plus a separate body with internal and terminal underscores for the attributed scanner alphabet. Bare and Bearer copies and one-character length, alphabet, case and adjacency mutations defend the supported contract; public IDs and redacted values remain negative. No provider response key or TruffleHog credential was copied or validated online.
